newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK SHARES FALL, SPOOKED BY TELECOM OTE DOWNTURN.
newsitem.headline: GREEK SHARES FALL, SPOOKED BY TELECOM OTE DOWNTURN.

text.p: Greek shares were at the mercy of telecom OTE's shares, 2.2 percent down, on Wednesday on persisting concerns over the unexpected downturn on the back of the successful part-float of OTE.
"Investors were disappointed to see a weak performance following the success of its part-float," said Mathios Doulos, a broker at Kyranis Securities.
"It was a panic-driven sell-off with no fundamental grounds for the shift in investor confidence," said a floor trader.
The unexpected downturn in OTE and large caps prompted investors who were buying in the previous sessions to reverse positions.
"Investors who were buying stock last week counting on a positive market sentiment were forced to square their positions, mounting considerable selling pressure," said Doulos.
Banks and major industrials went down in tandem with OTE on profit-taking because stocks in that sector have offered considerable gains during this year's rally, he added.

OTE's second part-flotation of 53.4 million shares -- 12.66 percent of its capital -- was oversubscribed three times, with foreign institutionals snapping up nearly half of the issue and global coordinators sizing down the allocation to some 245,000 retail investors to 80 shares.
The session provided the battling ground of institutional players for OTE's shares with heavy selling pressure countered by support at 6,600 drachmas.
"There was focused pressure on OTE's stock, but clear support with large bid sizes was present at 6,600 drachmas, the institutional book-building strike price," Doulos said.
Other brokers said there was foreign selling in OTE shares on Wednesday.

Starting today, OTE taps the market with a 7.5 percent, 190 billion drachma rights issue of 31.6 million shares at 6,000 drachmas each, entitling existing shareholders to six new shares per 80 outstanding.
But part-floated shares through last week's institutional book-building and public offering do not participate in the rights issue.
The Greek State offers retail investors with small shareholdings the option to purchase up to an additional four shares in order to acquire a minimum trading lot of ten shares.
The Athens general index gave up a net 2.30 percent or 36.37 points to close at 1,541.58 from Tuesday's 1,577.95 close, fluctuating between a nadir at 1,518.08 and the opening value of 1,569.28.
Banks and industrials led the market on the downside, receding 2.42 and 2.62 percent, respectively.
Turnover was helped by active trading in OTE which amounted to 5.1 billion drachmas. It totalled 21.2 billion on volume of 4.1 million shares.
Decliners led advancers 179 to 42 with 21 shares unchanged on 242 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted at London's SEAQ International market at $12.25-$12.30. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.

The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 1,112-1,142 drachmas. Shares of the underlying instrument were off 148 drachmas at 6,615, trading ex-rights.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 528.05-561.75 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $70.60-$72.30. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,181-3,396 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $12.50-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 208-239 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
